sections.h2: Who bills tax on a Waco house
sections.html:
Three parties shape a Waco bill. McLennan Central Appraisal District decides value, every taxing unit chooses its own rate, and the McLennan County Tax Office sends the statement and takes payment.

About 147,788 people live in Waco, and 49.4 percent of homes are owner-occupied. The median owned home is worth $221,700, and median rent is $1,165. Since roughly half of homes are rentals, plenty of Waco owners are landlords, and a rental house takes no homestead exemption.

One Waco address can sit inside several taxing units at once: McLennan County, McLennan Community College, a school district and the City of Waco, plus a Waco improvement district at $0.100000. The school unit depends on the address. Besides Waco ISD, the county lists Midway, Connally, La Vega, China Spring, Lorena and several other districts, so check which one is on your account.

  • Values, exemptions, protests: McLennan Central Appraisal District, 315 S 26th Street, Waco. Homestead exemptions can be filed through its online portal.
  • Bills and payments: McLennan County Tax Office.
  • City rate and budget: the City of Waco finance department.

The City of Waco's 2026 rate is $0.755000 per $100 of taxable value, made up of $0.578371 for operations and $0.176629 for debt service. The 2026-2027 budget keeps the rate at 75.5000 cents.

The city projects a $73.75 decrease on the average household's property tax bill and an extra $7.97 a year in utility and fee changes. The total operating budget is $733.3 million. With the rate unchanged, any move in your city bill comes from your own taxable value.

Each unit's total splits into operations and debt. Waco ISD's $1.034870 is $0.763700 for operations and $0.271170 for debt. The county's $0.374805 is $0.344706 and $0.030099, and the college's $0.140715 is $0.123438 and $0.017277.

Your own combined rate depends on your school district and any special district.

A Waco bill can be paid as soon as it arrives. It turns delinquent once January 31 of the next year goes by, and a weekend January 31 pushes the due date to the next business day.

Texas's late schedule governs. February 1 begins a 6% penalty and 1% interest. The penalty swells each month until it hits 12% on July 1, and interest has no ceiling. A unit that hires a collection attorney may add up to 20%. Seniors, disabled owners and a disabled veteran may pay in four installments.

  • October: bills go out from the tax office.
  • November 30: first-half deadline if you split the bill, with the balance due by the next June 30.
  • January 31: the general due date for the full amount.
  • February 1: penalty and interest begin.

Online payment needs only your property tax account number. For in-person and mail options, ask the tax office. A vendor operates the payment site, so direct any site questions to the tax office too.

The vendor keeps a 2.19% fee on cards and a flat $1.50 on electronic checks. Cards need just the account number, while an e-check also needs bank details. Visa, Mastercard, Discover and American Express are accepted.

The tax office runs tax sales online through GovEase, where bidders register. An owner facing a sale should ask the tax office about redemption, which Texas limits by property type.

sections.h2: Lowering your appraisal or tax bill
sections.html:
Two levers exist. Live in the house and you can file for the homestead exemption. Think the value is high and you can protest it. Both go through the appraisal district, and most exemption forms are due before May 1.

Owners whose market value climbed by $1,000 or more get a notice of appraised value from McLennan CAD. Three figures appear on it. Market value is the January 1 selling price estimate, assessed value reflects the homestead cap, and taxable value is what is left once exemptions come off.

  • Deadline: May 15, or 30 days after mailing if that is later.
  • Filing: by email, at 315 S 26th Street, or in the online portal that opens April 10 and closes May 15 for most residential property.
  • Next: an informal meeting with a district appraiser, then a review board hearing if you cannot settle.
  • Representation: a relative or friend can act for you with an appointment of agent form.

Upload evidence through the portal using the owner ID and PIN printed on your notice. The board weighs market value, so bring nearby comparable sales and photos of condition problems. After the first year, homestead value growth is capped at 10% annually, and seniors or disabled owners can freeze school tax.

sections.h2: Selling a Waco house with the tax bill
sections.html:
The year's tax lien is in place from January 1, so at closing the title company pays it and prorates the remainder.

Whoever owned on January 1 stays liable for that year, even if the sale closes in spring, and delinquent tax keeps title from clearing. A seller who is behind should request a balance covering county, city, school district and college. Heirs of a Waco home who are missing from the recorded deed can still claim the exemption with an ownership affidavit and a death certificate.

Because about half of Waco's homes are rented, a seller with a tenant should check whether a homestead exemption was ever filed. A rental carries none, so the seller's bill may run higher than neighbors' bills on owner-occupied homes.

First, get a balance for every unit from the county tax office. Second, confirm your exemption and your latest appraisal notice with the appraisal district. A rental will prompt buyer questions about what the tax runs without a homestead.

Give those numbers to your title company early so it can prorate the year, pay anything delinquent from proceeds and order a mortgage payoff. Cash buyers skip the lender, yet liens and tax still get paid before the deed moves. Get the closing date and any repair terms in writing from every buyer. If the house is vacant or inherited, say so at the start, since that changes what paperwork the title company needs and how fast closing can move.

faqs.q: What is the Waco city property tax rate?
faqs.a: $0.755000 per $100 of taxable value for 2026, split between $0.578371 for operations and $0.176629 for debt. The city's budget keeps it at 75.5000 cents.

faqs.q: What is the Waco ISD homestead exemption?
faqs.a: $140,000 for a homestead, rising to $200,000 for seniors and disabled owners, on a Waco ISD total rate of 1.034870.

faqs.q: Is there a penalty for paying Waco property tax in February?
faqs.a: Yes. Whatever remains after January 31 is delinquent, with 6% penalty and 1% interest starting February 1 and the penalty climbing monthly to 12% by July.

faqs.q: Can I protest my McLennan County appraisal online?
faqs.a: For most residential property, yes. The portal is open April 10 through May 15, the filing deadline, unless a later date applies 30 days after mailing.

faqs.q: Does a Waco rental house get a homestead exemption?
faqs.a: No. Only an owner living there as a main residence on January 1 qualifies, and no second homestead may be claimed elsewhere. Rentals are taxed in full.
